transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-06-25 15:00 PDT, Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rafael (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Dr. Anika Rao (CISO, Pinnacle), James Liu (CTO), Samir Patel (Head of IT), Holly Grant (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick run through of data handling assurances. Main asks: formal no-train commitment, options for ephemeral prompt retention, KMS key control, SOC 2 evidence, and on-prem integration checklist.

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account. Rafael is our solutions engineer, Lena will handle the pilot/setup and contract items.
[00:12] Dr. Anika Rao: Thanks, Maya. We just want to be very clear up front about training on customer data. For clinical notes we cannot have any of that used to retrain models, that's a firm requirement.
[00:24] Rafael: Absolutely, agreed. Redwood's standard hosted offering has a "no-training" option for customer data at the tenancy level — in that mode we don't persist prompts for model training. We can also enable ephemeral prompt handling so prompts don't hit long-term logs.
[00:41] James Liu: Sorry, just to clarify, is that a contractual guarantee or a config flag? We need attestation for audits.
[00:48] Maya: Good question. It's both — we have a contractual addendum we can sign that states we don't use customer prompts for model training, and operationally we configure a tenancy and routing policy that ensures data marked as no-train is excluded from any training pipelines. We'll send the wording and SOC 2 docs.
[01:06] Samir Patel: What's the default retention timeframe if we don't enable ephemeral mode? We have to be mindful of logs for troubleshooting.
[01:12] Rafael: Default logs are 30 days for request/response metadata and 90 days for some trace artifacts, but customers can opt into ephemerality and shorter retention. There's also an option to store only hashed metadata for debugging.
[01:30] Holly Grant: For product we still want metrics like latency and error rates, is that preserved if prompts are ephemeral?
[01:36] Rafael: Yes, we preserve aggregated telemetry (counts, latencies) but strip raw prompt content when ephemerality is enabled. You get the same observability dashboards — token-level cost is still tracked but content is redacted.
[01:48] Speaker 2: (mumbled) how about PII in the prompt — do you offer PII masking?
[01:54] Rafael: We do. We offer client-side pseudonymization libraries for common PII/PHI patterns, and server-side redaction hooks. We typically recommend client-side pseudonymization before sending sensitive fields; if you want us to manage it we can discuss data processing agreements.
[02:12] Dr. Anika Rao: KMS is critical. We cannot have Redwood manage the master keys. We need customer-managed KMS with hardware-backed key storage ideally.
[02:21] Maya: Understood. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for hosted and Dedicated offerings. For Private deploys we can integrate with on-prem HSMs — we have a KMS integration guide we'll share.
[02:35] James Liu: If we use customer-managed KMS in hosted mode, do you still see plaintext in your logs or traces?
[02:42] Rafael: No, encryption is envelope-based. Payloads are encrypted with a data key that is itself encrypted with your CMK. Redwood only sees encrypted blobs; we store encrypted artifacts but we can still provide limited metadata for billing and SLOs. We can provide an architecture diagram demonstrating that flow.
[02:59] Samir Patel: For SOC 2/ISO evidence, what artifacts do you provide for vendor assessments? We need the report and the control mappings.
[03:08] Maya: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 summary where available, plus a mapping spreadsheet showing controls mapped to customer concerns (SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, incident response). I'll send that after the call.
[03:22] Holly Grant: On SSO — we use Okta and enforce SCIM groups. Does Redwood support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning?
[03:29] Rafael: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is enforced at the route and token level; we can create role templates for auditors, devs, and operators.
[03:42] Dr. Anika Rao: Audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for who accessed what prompts and when. Is that possible while preserving ephemerality?
[03:50] Rafael: We can provide immutable audit metadata (user, timestamp, resource id, operation) without storing the full prompt content. That satisfies audit traceability while retaining prompt ephemerality. We can also forward audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or API.
[04:06] James Liu: If audit logs are forwarded, is there PII in those logs?
[04:11] Rafael: We redact PII by default if ephemerality is on; logs contain identifiers but not raw PII/PHI. You can also opt-in to keep certain fields if needed for compliance, but that would change the data handling classification.
[04:26] Maya: Just to make sure — you're looking for a written attestation that Redwood will not use your prompts for training, KMS integration details, SOC 2 report, and an ephemeral prompts config guide, correct?
[04:34] Dr. Anika Rao: Correct, and also a short runbook for our infra team to integrate our on-prem proxies and firewall rules for the private deployment option.
[04:41] Rafael: We'll include an on-prem checklist — network ports, certs, proxy headers, and required outbound endpoints. We also have a light-weight single-node trial package if you want to validate locally.
[04:55] Holly Grant: Are there extra charges for enabling no-train / ephemeral modes?
[05:00] Maya: No extra charge for the configuration. If you choose Private or Dedicated modes that have different pricing, that will be on the contract. Ephemerality is a configuration toggle for hosted tenants.
[05:10] Samir Patel: For our security review we'll need a contact for incident response and a playbook. Do you have SLAs for incident notification?
[05:16] Maya: Yes, enterprise customers get incident notifications as part of the contract — 24/7 on-call, with initial notification windows by severity. We can share our IR playbook redacted for customer privacy.
[05:29] James Liu: Can you walk briefly through how Redwood handles model fallbacks? Suppose a model is unavailable and you route to a smaller variant — will the smaller model receive the same no-train guarantee?
[05:39] Rafael: Good question. Fallbacks inherit the same tenancy-level policies. The no-train attribute is attached to the request metadata and is honored by any serving variant we route to. We'll show the routing policy YAML in the runbook.
[05:52] Dr. Anika Rao: For our auditors, will you sign a clause that allows us to audit your controls or request evidence?
[05:58] Maya: We can provide SOC 2 reports and supporting artifacts and accept reasonable audit requests through a VSA process; full on-site audits are handled case-by-case. We'll outline the evidence package.
[06:10] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:17] Rafael: Also, we have a technical option called "prefix/KV cache masking" so customer-specific prefixes can be kept out of shared caches; that reduces spillover into telemetry while improving caching.
[06:30] Samir Patel: If we go with a Private deployment, can we use our HSM and fully isolate networking?
[06:36] Rafael: Yes. Private includes VPC-only communication, optional air-gapped on-prem packaging, and HSM integration. For HIPAA-covered data we usually recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
[06:49] Holly Grant: What's the time to spin up a Dedicated pool? We may need throughput guarantees for production.
[06:55] Maya: Dedicated provisioning is 4-6 weeks for initial capacity, subject to GPU availability. We can provide burst capacity temporarily during onboarding.
[07:05] James Liu: Any limitations on model auditing — for example, could we request a dump of training corpus to validate there's no overlap?
[07:13] Rafael: We can't provide model training data dumps for open models; however, for Redwood-verified internal workflows we can provide provenance reports and model lineage docs that show sources. For the no-train case, there is no merge of your prompts into training corpora.
[07:29] Dr. Anika Rao: Can you confirm in writing that prompt content marked no-train is not used to update any model weights or training pipelines?
[07:36] Maya: Yes, we'll include explicit contractual language: prompts labeled "no-train" or tenant-level flags will not be used for training. We'll provide a sample clause.
[07:45] Holly Grant: About data residency — our production patient data must stay in us-east-1. Is regional pinning available?
[07:51] Rafael: Yes, we support region pinning at the tenancy level. Hosted tenants can be pinned to a region; Dedicated and Private obviously run in customer-chosen regions or on-prem.
[08:03] Samir Patel: Are there any telemetry tradeoffs when pinning region — e.g., global dashboards will still aggregate but raw logs stay in region?
[08:10] Rafael: We keep raw logs and prompt content within the pinned region. Aggregated metrics can be rolled up to a global console but without raw content leaving region. For regulated environments we suggest keeping even metrics routing regional.
[08:22] James Liu: For the pilot, we'd like to run a short benchmark around latency with a 512-token average request and measure tail latency at p95/p99. Can Redwood provide a runner or do you want us to run?
[08:33] Rafael: We can provide a small test runner and a script; we also recommend running it from your infra to capture egress hops. We'll include the benchmark script in the runbook.
[08:45] Maya: Okay, wrapping up — we'll send SOC 2, KMS diagram, ephemeral prompts guide, on-prem checklist, and the pilot NDA. Any final questions?
[08:55] Dr. Anika Rao: One more: do you have a sample DPA that includes HIPAA addendum language?
[09:00] Maya: We have a HIPAA appendix we can include in the DPA for covered customers. I'll route that to Lena to attach to the NDA.
[09:08] Lena Wu: I'll follow up with the DPA and HIPAA appendix.
[09:12] James Liu: Thanks everyone, we'll review and get back with preferred dates for the infra call.
[09:18] Maya: Great, thanks all. We'll send the materials today and check back in early next week.

End transcript.

Notes: Occasional transcription errors and speaker mislabels (typical of auto transcripts). References to docs: SOC 2 report (link to be provided), KMS integration diagram (attachment), ephemeral-prompts-runbook.md (attachment), pilot NDA (link).
